data.name: Faq_Q1_Title
data.value: Device Not Detected (No devices detected / Empty list)

data.name: Faq_Q1_Symptom
data.value: The device ComboBox remains empty or displays 'No devices detected'.

data.name: Faq_Q1_Cause
data.value: Damaged or charge-only USB cable, USB debugging disabled on phone, missing Samsung USB drivers (Windows), or missing udev rules (Linux).

data.name: Faq_Q1_Solution
data.value: 1. On phone: Settings > Developer Options > enable 'USB Debugging'. 2. Windows: Install official Samsung Mobile USB Composite driver. 3. Linux: Run 'sudo usermod -aG plugdev $USER' and reload udev. 4. Connect directly to PC motherboard USB port using a verified data cable.

data.name: Faq_Q2_Symptom
data.value: Phone appears in the device list with 'unauthorized' status and Start session button is disabled.

data.name: Faq_Q2_Cause
data.value: The PC RSA cryptographic handshake prompt was not accepted on the smartphone display.

data.name: Faq_Q2_Solution
data.value: 1. Unlock your phone screen. 2. On the USB debugging authorization popup, check 'Always allow from this computer' and tap 'Allow'. 3. If prompt does not appear: Developer Options > tap 'Revoke USB debugging authorizations' and reconnect cable.

data.name: Faq_Q3_Title
data.value: ADB Version Conflict (adb server version doesn't match this client)

data.name: Faq_Q3_Symptom
data.value: Execution console displays cyclic 'killing adb server...' logs or crashes.

data.name: Faq_Q3_Cause
data.value: Another program (Android Studio, Samsung Smart Switch, emulator) is spawning a conflicting adb.exe version on port 5037.

data.name: Faq_Q3_Solution
data.value: 1. Close background emulators, Android Studio, and Smart Switch. 2. Open Task Manager and terminate conflicting adb.exe processes. 3. In ScrcpyDeX settings, configure an absolute unified ADB executable path.

data.name: Faq_Q4_Title
data.value: Failed to Allocate DeX Virtual Display

data.name: Faq_Q4_Symptom
data.value: Session aborts with 'Failed to allocate Samsung DeX virtual display ID' in terminal logs.

data.name: Faq_Q4_Cause
data.value: Incompatible device (Galaxy A/M/Z Flip series lack DeX desktop virtualization hardware), screen locked with pending Knox biometric unlock, or previous session stuck.

data.name: Faq_Q4_Solution
data.value: 1. Verify device compatibility (Galaxy S, Note, Z Fold, and Tab S series only). 2. Unlock phone screen before clicking 'START DEX SESSION'. 3. Click 'Stop Session' or 'Rescan' to forcefully terminate orphan virtual display instances.

data.name: Faq_Q5_Title
data.value: Server JAR Deployment Error (scrcpydex-server.jar not found)

data.name: Faq_Q5_Symptom
data.value: FileNotFoundException or adb push failure when starting session.

data.name: Faq_Q5_Cause
data.value: scrcpydex-server.jar file is missing or Android /data/local/tmp has corrupted permissions or insufficient storage.

data.name: Faq_Q5_Solution
data.value: 1. Clean corrupted target files by executing: adb shell rm -f /data/local/tmp/scrcpydex-server.jar 2. Verify free storage space on internal phone memory.

data.name: Faq_Q6_Symptom
data.value: Log shows 'ERROR: Could not create renderer: D3D11CreateDevice (DXGI_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED)'.

data.name: Faq_Q6_Cause
data.value: Host GPU lacks DirectX 11 Feature Level 10_0 support, or running inside a VM / Remote Desktop (RDP) session without 3D acceleration.

data.name: Faq_Q6_Solution
data.value: 1. Under Display Parameters & Encoder, change 'Render Driver' to 'OpenGL'. 2. Update GPU display drivers directly from AMD, Intel, or NVIDIA website.

data.name: Faq_Q7_Title
data.value: Missing Hardware Acceleration on Linux (VA-API / Mesa)

data.name: Faq_Q7_Symptom
data.value: High CPU usage, frame skipping, or video rendering stuttering on Linux.

data.name: Faq_Q7_Cause
data.value: VA-API hardware video decoding drivers are missing from the Linux operating system.

data.name: Faq_Q7_Solution
data.value: Install VA-API acceleration packages via terminal: sudo apt install va-driver-all i965-va-driver intel-media-va-driver vainfo mesa-va-drivers

data.name: Faq_Q8_Title
data.value: Black Screen or Video Artifacts (Blocky pixels / Distortion)

data.name: Faq_Q8_Symptom
data.value: scrcpy window opens but shows a black screen or distorted pixel blocks.

data.name: Faq_Q8_Cause
data.value: H.265/AV1 selected on a GPU with only H.264 hardware decoding, or bitrate exceeds USB connection bandwidth.

data.name: Faq_Q8_Solution
data.value: 1. Switch 'Video Codec' to 'h264'. 2. Set Resolution to '1920x1080 (FHD)' and Framerate to 30 or 60 fps. 3. Lower Transmission Bitrate preset to 12 or 18 Mbps.

data.name: Faq_Q9_Title
data.value: Mouse Pointer Lag or Double Cursor (aoa vs uhid)

data.name: Faq_Q9_Symptom
data.value: Cursor has perceptible delay or two mouse pointers appear simultaneously.

data.name: Faq_Q9_Cause
data.value: Native UHID mouse emulation disabled, falling back to Android touch injection (AOA/SDK).

data.name: Faq_Q9_Solution
data.value: 1. Enable 'Native UHID Mouse' in Quick Session Options. 2. On Linux: Ensure user has read/write permissions to /dev/uhid by being part of the plugdev group.

data.name: Faq_Q10_Title
data.value: Desktop Shortcuts Not Reaching DeX (Alt+Tab, Windows Key)

data.name: Faq_Q10_Symptom
data.value: Pressing Alt+Tab or Windows key switches host computer windows instead of DeX apps.

data.name: Faq_Q10_Cause
data.value: Forward Shortcut Keys option is disabled, or running under Wayland without modifier key capture.

data.name: Faq_Q10_Solution
data.value: 1. Enable 'Forward Shortcut Keys' in Quick Session Options. 2. On Linux: Use an X11 / Xorg desktop session for full modifier key forwarding.

data.name: Faq_Q11_Title
data.value: Audio Noise, Crackling, or Delay (Sample rate mismatch)

data.name: Faq_Q11_Symptom
data.value: Audio is crackling, popping, or out of sync with video playback.

data.name: Faq_Q11_Cause
data.value: Sample rate divergence between Android output (48,000 Hz) and PC audio output (e.g. 44,100 Hz).

data.name: Faq_Q11_Solution
data.value: 1. In Windows Sound settings > Output device properties: set Default Format to 24-bit 48000 Hz or 16-bit 48000 Hz. 2. Enable 'Low Latency Audio' in Quick Session Options. 3. Select 'Opus 48kHz Stereo' as audio codec.

data.name: Faq_Q12_Title
data.value: Phone Overheating & Fast Battery Drain During Sessions

data.name: Faq_Q12_Symptom
data.value: Temperature meter turns amber/red (> 40°C) and battery discharges quickly while connected.

data.name: Faq_Q12_Cause
data.value: Physical AMOLED phone screen stays on at high brightness while the GPU renders the desktop interface.

data.name: Faq_Q12_Solution
data.value: 1. Enable 'Turn off mobile screen' in Quick Session Options. 2. Phone screen shuts off completely, reducing temperature by up to 8°C and preventing OLED burn-in. 3. Connect phone to a USB 3.0 port capable of delivering adequate power (1.5A to 3A).
